actions.action: Remove affected leaves with sterilized scissors and bag them for disposal
Trim any rotten roots if found
Repot into fresh chunky aroid mix in a clean pot with drainage holes
Check soil and water only when top 2-3 inches are dry
Test fungicide on one leaf first
Apply copper, chlorothalonil or mancozeb fungicide per label if spots keep appearing
Check leaf undersides and stems for pests
Isolate the plant from other plants
Photograph roots and leaf undersides and share them

reason: The answer correctly names fungal leaf spot as the main cause and recommends removing affected leaves, but makes the fungicide that resolved it conditional and buries it among repotting and care changes; none of the advice is likely to cause harm.
